statement: Let n = len(nums). Call a pair (i,j) of integers valid when 0 <= i < n, 0 <= j < n, |i-j| >= indexDifference, and |nums[i]-nums[j]| >= valueDifference. Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = 2 and: (1) if at least one valid pair exists, then 0 <= r[0] < n, 0 <= r[1] < n, |r[0]-r[1]| >= indexDifference, and |nums[r[0]]-nums[r[1]]| >= valueDifference; (2) if no valid pair exists, then r[0] = -1 and r[1] = -1. Any valid ordered pair is acceptable; the specification does not require a unique answer.
preconditions: Let n = len(nums). The input satisfies 1 <= n <= 100; for every k with 0 <= k < n, 0 <= nums[k] <= 50; 0 <= indexDifference <= 100; and 0 <= valueDifference <= 50. All I64 values are interpreted as mathematical integers; these bounds keep the mentioned differences and absolute values in range.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail.
